title: Minimum Distance Between Three Equal Elements I
summary: Given an integer array, find the minimum distance of any triplet of indices where the values at those indices are equal.
statement: Given an integer array, find the minimum distance of any triplet of indices where the values at those indices are equal. If no such triplet exists, return -1.
constraints: Choose three increasing indices containing the same value.
Their distance is the sum of all three pairwise index distances.
Return the minimum distance, or -1 if no equal-value triplet exists.
hints: For ordered i<j<k, pairwise distance simplifies to 2*(k-i).
For one value, only consecutive triples can minimize the outer span.
Evaluate those triples across groups and return the smallest result.
editorial: Evaluate those triples across groups and return the smallest result.

tests.explanation: Indices zero, two, and three hold one; their pairwise distances total six.
No value occurs three times, so return -1.
